title: Overexpose
description: A summer sky through a pine, developed live on colour negative film. Drag up to overexpose it by as much as three stops. A phone sensor would clip the clouds to flat white; the negative's long shoulder and the print paper's toe fold the light in instead, so the cobalt thins to powder blue, the shadows open into pastel, and the cumulus keep their shape all the way up. Halation and diffusion grow as the shadows they land on lift out of the toe.
intent: Genre spec idea 5, after Rinko Kawauchi's overexposed 6x6 colour (Utatane, Illuminance): show why film looks dreamy and digital looks cheap with one gesture, exposure, on real linear radiance through per-layer H&D curves and a print curve. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinko_Kawauchi
sources: HDRI: Tree Lined Driveway, Poly Haven, photographed by Dimitrios Savva, processed by Jarod Guest, CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/tree_lined_driveway (8k .hdr: https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/8k/tree_lined_driveway_8k.hdr). Worm's-eye view lying under the pines: stereographic projection, 116 deg field, pitched +76 deg towards the zenith at yaw +150 deg from the panorama centre, rolled -10 deg, 1536 px square. The sun is moved behind the top-centre pine. No camera aim can do that (in this HDRI it stands in open sky about 20 deg from the nearest crown, and turning the camera carries the crown along), so its disc, 16-ray diffraction star and aureole are painted out of the equirect, then the frame's open sky is fitted as an elevation gradient plus a radial term around the old sun, and only the radial term is moved to a new direction 2 deg inside that crown's lower edge, with the measured, ray-free circumsolar excess added there, on sky pixels only with a 1-2 px feather. Around the sun the crown is rebuilt as a hard silhouette at its own dark density, and needles on its open-sky edge in the sun's forward lobe get a thin (about 2 px) warm-white transmitted rim, scaled to outshine the sky beyond. The pale ghost the painted-out sun still left is removed in the camera frame: on open sky 10-48 deg from the new sun (thin cloud excluded by its whiteness against the fit), the sky is replaced by the fitted elevation gradient with no old-sun radial term, and the photograph's grain is re-added, matched in amplitude, grain size and channel correlation from open sky far from both suns. Then the open sky's smooth field is refitted and replaced by one that depends on zenith angle alone, darkest and most saturated overhead (printing about #2f6fc0 at 0 EV) and paler towards the low sky at the frame's edges, times a tight circumsolar glow around the hidden sun; only each pixel's sky share takes the change (read from blue-over-red chroma, and from luminance on the rim), so needles, the rim and cloud keep their light and the photograph's grain rides along as a ratio. The sky therefore deepens towards the zenith instead of paling towards an empty patch. The canopy's edges are then decontaminated: within 6 px of the open sky (and in the lit pockets of the crown around the hidden sun) each pixel's sky share is read from luminance between the local needle colour and the old sky behind it, the needle colour is solved as (C - t S_old) / (1 - t) and the pixel re-composited over the new sky, so the old pale sky no longer outlines the crowns in cream. Shipped as log2 radiance -8.5..+2.5 in 8 bits with TPDF dither (scene.webp), with the diffusion and halation blurs baked from the same radiance (optics.png). Last, the cumulus are relit: each pixel's cloud share is keyed from the scene (neutral and bright), blurred to the scale of puffs and banks, and the side of each blob that faces the frame's edge (away from the zenith, read from the blurred key's gradient) is multiplied towards skylight blue (#b8cde6), as is the part of a bank that more cloud shades from the hidden sun, while the sun-facing tops get a slight warm lift; the key ships as scene.webp's alpha, so the piece can hold everything but the cloud back as it overexposes and the clouds climb the print's shoulder above the sky. Last, the hidden sun is lit again, about 2-3 stops above what the earlier steps left of it: a near-white cyan aureole on the sky share around it (12x the local sky at the sun, falling off over 1.6 and 7 deg), a few sharp, un-blurred sparkles of the disc in the crown's real pin-hole gaps within 4 deg (one hot pixel and a faint short glint each), the crown's own needle mass deepened about 0.6 stop around the sun so it prints as the darkest silhouette in the frame, and, on the crown's open-sky edge in the sun's forward lobe, a transmitted fringe feathered over about 4 px into the needles: its light is the sky and aureole behind it (so cyan-white, not a colour of its own), scaled by the needles' local sky share and never more than 85% of that light, and mixed edge pixels take the aureole in their sky share, so the crown's lower lip ramps into the bloom instead of being outlined (an earlier 1.5 px warm-white rim printed as a crisp tan outline). The diffusion and halation are rebaked from that brighter light, and the disc's own light, which the encoding cannot hold, is added to the diffusion as a tight cyan-white veil around the hidden sun (falling off over 2.2 deg), weighted by the sky share (widened by the fringe, so it crosses the crown's lip) so it lands on the open sky around the crown and the needle mass keeps only 15% of it. The glow is keyed into the alpha as well (falling off over 9 deg, on the sky share; the needles take a fifth of it), so the printer's hold spares it: at 0 EV the crown is a dark silhouette with a glowing edge in a cyan-white bloom, and as the exposure rises the glow climbs the shoulder and swallows the crown's edge. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/overexpose (desun.py, resun.py, deepen.py, bake_wormseye.py, relight.py, sunburst.py).
